narrative.overview:
Everything in Lectern is arranged around one vertical column of screen. Two hairlines and a tick mark it, the pivot letter of every word lands on it, and no other element is allowed to compete with it while words are moving. The rail is not decoration; it is the product's mechanism drawn at full size.

Around that column the interface is deliberately thin. Type is monospace so every word occupies a predictable width, surfaces separate by tone rather than by ornament, and colour appears in one place at a time. When reading starts, the controls fade to 40% and the word is the only thing at full strength.

Two implementations share this world: Material 3 and Material You on Android, a hand-written CSS world on the web. The rail, the pivot, the fade and the monospace measure are what make them the same product.
keyCharacteristics: One reading column, marked by rails and a tick, that nothing else may cross
Monospace everywhere, so word width is predictable and numbers align
One accent at a time, spent on the pivot letter first
Chrome that fades to 40% while reading and returns on pause
Depth by tone, never by ornament
Dark is the working default; light is a real scheme, not an inversion

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber belongs to the pivot letter first. Any other use must be one element the eye can find without searching. Two amber elements competing on one screen is a defect.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Greys are warm, held in the amber family. A neutral grey next to this amber reads as a bug, not a choice.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: The pivot letter's centre sits at 50% of the stage width. Type size is derived from the chunk, never the other way round.

rules.name: The Italic Title Rule
rules.body: A book's own title is italic in the reader's top bar. It is the one italic in the system.

rules.name: The Undisturbed Stage Rule
rules.body: The reading surface carries no elevation, no border and no card. It is the page ground with two hairlines on it.

dos: Do keep the pivot centred at 50% of the stage and derive type size from the chunk, shrinking to fit rather than moving the column.
Do fade the reader's chrome to 40% while words are moving, and bring it back at full strength on pause.
Do spend amber on one element per screen, the pivot first.
Do state a value in numbers next to its control (300 wpm, \u00d72.7, 2 words), in monospace so it does not shift as it changes.
Do use Material components as they come and theme them through colour roles, so Material You and the four palettes both work untouched.
Do give every setting a description in the product's voice: what it does, and why a reader would want it.
donts: Don't draw a shadow, a border or a card around the reading stage.
Don't put a second accent-coloured element beside the pivot while reading.
Don't introduce a proportional face for the stage without keeping the fixed-column guarantee.
Don't use a neutral grey: greys here are warm and belong to the ground.
Don't add a bottom navigation bar. Three destinations on one back stack is the whole structure.
Don't interrupt reading with a dialog. Transient feedback is a snackbar; anything larger waits for a pause.
